candidates.name: Limited Systemic Scleroderma
support_spans: 20-year history of oral and ocular sicca symptoms
Raynaud phenomenon
Painless pinpoint white nodules present in the subcutaneous plane of the right fifth finger
Soft-tissue calcifications in the distal first and fifth fingers
Biopsy of digit lesions from right thumb and fourth finger consistent with calcinosis
Positive for antinuclear antibody 1:160 titer, nucleolar pattern, and anti-Ro
contradict_spans: No skin tightening, esophageal reflux, dysphagia, or telangiectasis reported
Previous skin biopsies showed no evidence of scleroderma
candidates.why: The patient's long history of sicca symptoms, Raynaud's phenomenon, and presence of calcinosis along with positive autoimmune serology are indicative of Limited Systemic Scleroderma.
